title: ExecutionReceipt v1
description: What a future AEF records after governing (and, if allowed, executing) an action. This is AEF OPERATIONAL TRUTH ('did AEF run this, under what policy decision, with what outcome') -- it is explicitly NOT Evidence & Trust's domain truth ('is this claim/entity verified'). Do not merge the two schemas even if they seem to overlap superficially; they answer different questions for different audiences and evolve independently (see README).

policy_decision.description: What the (future) AEF policy engine decided -- independent of and prior to actual execution outcome. A DENIED receipt records a request that was correctly refused; it is not a failure of the contract, it is proof the contract worked.

tool.description: Which tool/adapter actually performed the action, if any.

outcome.description: NOT_EXECUTED covers policy_decision=DENIED (nothing ran) as well as any consequential action correctly blocked by the failure model (Section 15) before execution.

verification_ref.description: Reference to independent evidence that the action actually happened as recorded (e.g. a re-query confirming state changed) -- distinct from the domain-truth verification Evidence & Trust would separately record.

deployment_identity.description: E.g. a commit SHA or deployed version identifier for whatever code executed this action -- ties an ExecutionReceipt back to Deployment/Runtime Truth (see docs/ive/OUT_OF_BAND_DEPLOYMENT_THREAT_MODEL.md from a prior mission).
